name: 2033 Prairie Avenue: the brick stable on the alley, K12
aka: the stable behind the Otis house, 2033 Prairie

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The draft's claim, kept: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Nothing else read dates it, so the range claims the 1904 target and no more. TO is the last day of the year the sheet was published, the latest date anything here shows it standing; it is not a demolition date.

placement.position_note: The middle of the building's alley (east) wall at grade, read off the committed sheet 35 raster (chicago/reference/prairie-avenue/sanborn-1911-and-robinson-1886/sanborn_1911_vol3_sheet_35.jpg) at pixel (1170.73, 825.93): the alley line by a median darkness profile over rows 810-842 (peak at column 1170.73; the building's alley wall is drawn on it), halfway between the north wall line (row 805.07, a profile over columns 1120-1160; the lot line west of the building reads row 805.01 on the same rule, so the wall is on the lot line) and the south wall line (row 846.79, the same columns; the lot line west of it reads 846.97), each peak refined by a parabola through the three highest samples. Carried to the local frame by the sheet's fitted similarity (data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_35_gcps.json): local E 1470.249, N -3584.939. The bearing is the parcel's (prairie_2033, data/street_grid/1904.json, -0.615 degrees, the draft's 179.385 less the half turn its plan frame took). The fit's own residual, 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of reading on this coarse copy, is all that is claimed.
placement.symbolic_location: 2033 S. Prairie Avenue, rear: east side of Prairie Avenue between 20th and 21st Streets, parcel prairie_2033 (data/street_grid/1904.json); on the rear lot line, its alley wall on the alley's west line, its north and south walls on the lot lines (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).

footprint.note: About the middle of the alley wall, u east (toward the alley, so the building lies at negative u) and v north. The sheet draws the building from the alley line (pixel column 1170.73) back to its west wall line (column 1091.59, a profile over rows 810-842): 79.15 pixels at the sheet's 0.185854 m a pixel, 14.710 m; and from its north wall line (row 805.07) to its south wall line (row 846.79): 41.72 pixels, 7.754 m along the alley. A plain rectangle: the sheet draws no step, wing or porch on it. The line 0.50 m north of 2031's north wall (row 760.08) is the south wall of 2027's barn; 2031's and 2033's buildings share the wall on row 805.07, and 2033's south wall on row 846.79 is shared with 2035's building.

stories.note: '2' lettered in the building's north-east corner, under its north wall line, as on 2031's. Built as the kit's carriage room (3.6 m) under a loft whose walls rise 2.7 m more to the eave, under a 30-degree roof dying into both party walls; those heights are RECONSTRUCTED. No dormer: the sheet draws none and the kit builds none.

construction.note: Drawn pink, the sheet's colour for brick. The small figures written inside its north and south wall lines are too coarse on this copy to read as wall thicknesses; the kit builds its own 13-inch walls.

value.note: Everything but the plan, the two storeys, the brick and the window mark's place is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-2033-stable-1938. The sheet gives the outline, '2' storeys, the brick, the label GARAGE, the alley wall on the alley line, the north wall on the lot line (row 805.01 west of the building) with 2031's garage, which stands against it on the same line, the south wall on the lot line (row 846.97 west of it) with 2035's building, which stands against it on the same line, the key's fire-wall ticks on the alley line at both of those junctions, one of the key's window marks on the alley wall (a cross with a dot for each storey, the sign 2011's and 2017's alley walls carry, its strokes over rows 824-834) 3.31 m from the south wall, and a solid dot inside the south-east corner (row 840.6; not built). The alley is on the EAST, so the kit is turned to face it (alley_side east). Both ends are party walls (east_end party), as 2011's stable is (L-k12-2011-stable-1938): the building stands on both lot lines with a fire-wall sign at each and a neighbour's building at or against each, so there is no open gable. On the alley wall, counted from the south party wall's inner face: a man door with a loft sash over it, the mark as a stable sash with a loft sash over it, and a carriage bay 3.0 m clear toward the north end, under the loft hatch and hoist; it is the only stretch of the alley wall north of the mark long enough for one. On the yard wall, counted from the north party wall's inner face: a stable sash toward the south end and a door, each with a loft sash over it, the door facing the house's two-storey brick rear range (its rear wall at column 1013.93, rows 805-832) 14.43 m west across the back yard. The workyard is the kit's: a brick apron 2.4 m wide along the yard wall and a walk from the yard door to that rear wall line. The roof is the kit's gable with the ridge along the alley at 30 degrees, the pitch 2011's 14.64 m deep stable takes, dying into both party walls; no dormer and no ventilator, as the sheet draws none. No ramp, stair, lean-to, wing or range: the sheet draws none.

coach_house.note: The building's dimensions are the footprint's (inferred, above); its openings, roof and loft are the kit's, laid out for this lot, and RECONSTRUCTED. See the value's own note for each choice and what bounds it.

function.note: Sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn draws a two-storey brick building on the alley behind 2033, uncrossed, and letters it GARAGE; 2031's, against it on the lot line they share, is drawn and lettered the same. GARAGE is the 1911 sheet's word and is not read as the 1904 use (the K12 kit's restriction no_1911_use_labels; T-1837 study ruling 11; the T-1842 census row s35-2033-rear backcasts the envelope and reconstructs the use as a stable/coach house). This record builds it as the house's stable and coach house: a carriage bay, a loft with its hatch and hoist, stable sash, and no motor-garage part. The use is RECONSTRUCTED; no source read names a horse, a carriage or a motor car on this lot.

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 35.
what_it_supplies: Footprints, lots and street widths from 20th to 22nd Street between Indiana and Calumet, as of 1911, at the copy's coarser resolution
The position of Twentieth Street, which is vacated between Indiana and Calumet today
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
Any lake edge: the sheet ends at Calumet Avenue

research_note: T-1938 refines the district draft (T-2352) in place under the same id onto the K12 coach-house kit, the seventh of the package's alley buildings on the east side of Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street, to leave the draft (2031's and 2033's together, in one PR). The sheet census (census row s35-2033-rear, trace s35fp-2033-b2) carries the building into 1904; the draft rules now skip that row. Read afresh off the committed sheet 35 raster by median darkness profiles rather than taken from the draft's fitted rectangle (14.0 x 7.25 m): the sheet draws a building 14.71 m deep from the alley line and 7.75 m along it, standing on both of its lot lines with a fire-wall sign at each end, and one window mark on its alley wall. This copy of the sheet is coarse (0.186 m a pixel), so every reading here carries about a pixel. Nothing read dates the building before the 1911 sheet; that it stood by 1904 is the census's carry-back, which the district draft already made. No picture of the alley behind the 2000 block is known to this project.
